chapter: Bird, the band's breakup and Luis Russell
title: Southern tour: promoters running off with the money
summary: In Augusta and Virginia, promoters vanished with receipts and the band paid out of pocket to avoid jail.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Now, we stayed -- they stayed in the band until we got back -- now, they sent us on a tour. I'm getting ahead of myself. We went on a tour to -- down South. And we played Augusta, ballroom in Augusta, and halftime the man left with the money. The cops came and made us -- we were either going to pay for that dance and pay for the cops -- pay for the rent of the hall and pay for the bouncers and the people on the door, or else we had to go to jail.

Now, we didn't book the dance. Somebody else hired us. But that man was gone, you know. So we had to take money out of our pockets to pay for that. So McShann -- the band started getting all disgusted, you know, going out and playing free and then giving, paying for the dance themselves, you know.

We got to Greens -- Green -- anyway, somewhere just outside of Martin -- might have been Martinville, Virginia, the same thing happened. And this time they were going to not only take us to jail, but they were going to take our instruments and the bus. This man had got away with the money again.

Yeah, it wasn't just Weinfield. Now, Weinfield was a good man. He's a Jewish man that had charge of this circuit, but now he would sell the band to somebody in some certain areas, you know. And so it wasn't him. In fact, if he'd known it, he would have, you know, taken care of it.

But anyway, we got back to New York. Everybody was mad by that time. And they booked us on a tour that carried us all the way out to Texas. When we got to Kansas City, Buddy, Charlie Bird Freddy Culver, Orville Minor, several of them quit, you know. Gus and I -- and there was only a few of us that stuck with Max Hand. McShann
